title: Python Mongo DB Update
text:
Python MongoDB
Update



Update Collection

You can update a record, or document as it is called in MongoDB, by using
the
update_one()
method.

The first parameter of the
update_one()
method
is a query object defining which document to update.

Note:
If the query finds more than one record, only the first
occurrence is updated.

The second parameter
is an object defining the new values of the document.

Example

Change the address from "Valley 345" to "Canyon 123":

import pymongo
myclient = pymongo.MongoClient("mongodb://localhost:27017/")

mydb = myclient["mydatabase"]
mycol = mydb["customers"]

myquery = { "address": "Valley 345" }
newvalues = { "$set": {
"address": "Canyon 123" } }

mycol.update_one(myquery, newvalues)
#print "customers" after the update:
for x in mycol.find():
print(x)

Run example »

Update Many

To update
all
documents that meets the criteria of the query, use
the
update_many()
method.

Example

Update all documents where the address starts with the letter "S":

import pymongo
myclient = pymongo.MongoClient("mongodb://localhost:27017/")

mydb = myclient["mydatabase"]
mycol = mydb["customers"]

myquery = { "address": { "$regex": "^S" } }
newvalues = { "$set": {
"name": "Minnie" } }

x = mycol.update_many(myquery, newvalues)
print(x.modified_count, "documents updated.")
